meta_title: Madmail · Chatmail relay for Delta Chat
meta_description: Madmail is a free, open-source chatmail relay for Delta Chat, written in Rust: encrypted mail only, federated, one binary to install. We care about secure communication.
og_alt: Madmail: chatmail relay for Delta Chat, on an airmail envelope
hero_pitch: Madmail is the server side of Delta Chat: a Rust relay that accepts, stores and federates end-to-end encrypted mail, shipped as one binary. We care about secure communication.
role_operators_line: Run your own relay on a Linux server, with a domain or just a public IP. One binary, TLS from Let's Encrypt.
role_users_line: Madmail carries Delta Chat messages between people. Accounts are created on first login, so there is no sign-up form.
role_phone_line: Madmail Mobile runs a Madmail relay on an Android phone for the people on its Wi-Fi or hotspot. No domain, no VPS.
role_devs_line: Madmail is Rust under AGPL-3.0-or-later. Read the code, the design notes and the admin API, then send a pull request.
letter_intro: Chatmail is how Delta Chat turns ordinary email into a fast, encrypted messenger. It works best when both ends use a chatmail relay. Madmail is one: a server built for that job alone, not a general-purpose mail server.
p_encrypted_body: The relay enforces a PGP-only policy. Unencrypted mail is rejected at the door.
p_jit_body: An account is created the first time a Delta Chat client logs in.
p_fed_body: Mail between relays travels over HTTPS through /mxdeliv, with SMTP as the fallback, so Madmail also reaches other chatmail relays and ordinary mail servers.
p_one_body: SMTP, IMAP, the admin API, call relays and certificates run in a single process. There is nothing else to install.
sort_lede: Madmail is the whole sorting office for chatmail. Each service a relay needs is a counter inside the one binary.
f_mail_body: Submission, incoming mail and retrieval: the full mail stack in one process.
f_pgp_body: Unencrypted mail is rejected at the server.
f_jit_body: No sign-up flow. Accounts are created on first login.
f_fed_body: /mxdeliv for fast delivery between relays, SMTP as the fallback.
f_nolog_body: Strip message metadata when strict privacy is required.
f_calls_body: Audio and video calls and the WebXDC realtime relay, with no extra services.
f_tls_body: Automatic certificates from Let's Encrypt, for a domain or a bare IP.
f_admin_body: Run the relay from the Madmail Admin web panel or the madmail command line; both use the same admin API.
route_lede: A message leaves Delta Chat already sealed. Madmail takes it in and hands it on to the other relay; only the two apps can open it.
route_app_note: Delta Chat encrypts the message on your device.
route_relay_note: Madmail accepts it over SMTP and refuses anything unencrypted.
route_fed_note: Relay to relay over HTTPS /mxdeliv, or SMTP as the fallback.
route_relay2_note: Any chatmail relay or mail server keeps it until it is fetched.
route_app2_note: Delta Chat fetches it over IMAP and decrypts it on their device.
route_key_admin: Madmail Admin: the web panel for running a relay.
route_key_mobile: Madmail Mobile: a relay on an Android phone, for its hotspot.
route_key_calls: TURN and Iroh: calls and WebXDC realtime, built in.
route_key_nolog: No-Log mode: metadata stripped where privacy demands it.
install_lede: Download the release binary for your machine, install it and start the service. Each slip is one way to deploy it.
slip_domain_note: DNS must point to your server. Let's Encrypt issues a standard certificate with a 90-day renewal.
slip_ip_note: No domain needed. Let's Encrypt issues an IP certificate with about a 6-day renewal; port 80 must be open.
install_other: On Windows 10 or 11, use madmail-windows-amd64-setup.exe from Releases. On Debian 12, Ubuntu 22.04 and Rocky Linux 9, download madmail-linux-amd64-legacy instead.
set_lede: Madmail comes with an app, a panel and the notes we keep while building it.
set_mobile_body: Host a Madmail relay on an Android phone, or manage your servers over SSH or the admin API.
set_mobile_alt: Madmail Mobile overview screen on Android
set_admin_body: The web panel for a running relay: accounts, settings and services.
set_releases_body: Release notes and downloads for every version.
faq_what_a: Madmail is a chatmail relay: the server that Delta Chat apps use to send, store and receive end-to-end encrypted messages. It is written in Rust and ships SMTP, IMAP, HTTP federation, an admin API and call relays as a single binary.
faq_general_q: Is it a general-purpose mail server?
faq_general_a: No. Madmail is built for how Delta Chat works. It only accepts end-to-end encrypted (OpenPGP) mail and rejects plaintext messages.
faq_domain_a: No. Madmail can run on a public IP address with a Let's Encrypt IP certificate, which renews about every 6 days and needs port 80. With a domain, it uses a standard 90-day certificate.
faq_accounts_a: Just in time: an account is created the first time a Delta Chat client logs in, so there is no separate sign-up flow.
faq_fed_q: Can it talk to other relays and mail servers?
faq_fed_a: Yes. Relays federate over HTTPS through /mxdeliv and fall back to SMTP, so Madmail interoperates with other chatmail relays and regular mail servers.
faq_os_q: Which systems does it run on?
faq_os_a: Linux on amd64 and arm64 with systemd, for example Debian 13, Ubuntu 24.04 and AlmaLinux 10, plus a legacy build for older glibc such as Debian 12. Windows 10 and 11 (x64) have an installer. Docker images are also available.
faq_calls_a: Yes. A TURN server and an Iroh relay are built in, for Delta Chat audio and video calls and WebXDC realtime, with no extra services to run.
faq_licence_q: What does it cost, and under which licence?
faq_licence_a: Madmail is free and open source under the AGPL-3.0-or-later licence. The source code is on GitHub.
footer_note: Free software under AGPL-3.0-or-later. Use at your own risk; validate it for your threat model before production use.
